candidate.answerReason: The midpoint of AE lies 5/2 inches from AD and 19/2 inches from BC. Parallel lines therefore divide PQ in the ratio 5:19.

methods.label: Transfer the ratio using parallel lines
methods.explanation:
The perpendicular bisector tells us that \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AE\). To locate that midpoint relative to the parallel sides \(AD\) and \(BC\), let \(H\) be the midpoint of \(DE\).

In triangle \(ADE\), the segment \(HM\) joins two side midpoints. The triangle midsegment theorem therefore gives \(HM\parallel AD\). Since opposite sides of a square are parallel, the three lines \(AD\), \(HM\), and \(BC\) are parallel.

On the top side of the square,
\[
DH=\frac{DE}{2}=\frac52,
\qquad
HC=DC-DH=12-\frac52=\frac{19}{2}.
\]
The three parallel lines meet the transversal \(DC\) at \(D,H,C\) and the transversal \(PQ\) at \(P,M,Q\), respectively. Corresponding segments cut by parallel lines are proportional, so
\[
\frac{PM}{MQ}=\frac{DH}{HC}
=\frac{5/2}{19/2}=\frac5{19}.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{PM:MQ=5:19}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: The proof uses only midpoints, square properties, triangle midsegments, and proportional segments cut by parallel lines.
